package application

import (
	"context"

	"metaldocs/internal/platform/authn"
)

// A3.3 negative fixture (Rule 2, INDIRECT via an alias of the CANONICAL
// accessor): the fresh gap after the E1 alias fix (PR #108 review round 1,
// finding 3).
//
// indirect_lowlevel_actor.go proved Rule 1 has to follow a reference through an
// alias, not just a call. This file proves Rule 2 has the same hole, on the
// OTHER accessor: `extract := authn.RequireUserID` binds the presence-aware,
// fail-closed function to a local, and `actor, _ := extract(ctx)` discards its
// error exactly as `actor, _ := authn.RequireUserID(ctx)` would — but
// ignoredPresenceViolation resolves call.Fun with isSelector, which requires a
// *ast.SelectorExpr. `extract(ctx)` has call.Fun as a bare *ast.Ident, so the
// direct-call check never fires, and the discard ships clean.
//
// This is not the low-level accessor Rule 1 already bans — authn.RequireUserID
// is the correct, fail-closed function, called correctly. The defect is one
// hop later: its own presence result is thrown away through an alias, which
// puts the "" straight back into the consumer Rule 2 exists to stop. A guard
// that only matches `authn.RequireUserID(ctx)` verbatim is a guard a one-line
// local assignment turns off.
//
// See scripts/testdata/guard-fixtures/README.md.
func chargeViaAliasedAccessor(ctx context.Context) string {
	extract := authn.RequireUserID
	actor, _ := extract(ctx)
	return actor
}

// The bool-returning sibling is pinned too: aliasing UserIDFromContext and
// discarding its presence bool through the alias is the same shape, one
// accessor over.
func settleViaAliasedAccessor(ctx context.Context) string {
	probe := authn.UserIDFromContext
	actor, _ := probe(ctx)
	return actor
}
